topic: The Rhythm of Change: Derivative Formulas and Geometric Intuition
target_audience: High school seniors or early university students beginning Calculus

outline.topic: The Rhythm of Change: Derivative Formulas and Geometric Intuition
outline.target_audience: High school seniors or early university students beginning Calculus

sections.title: The Hook: The Cheetah's Instantaneous Speed
sections.content: Introduce the difference between average speed and instantaneous speed. Use a narrative approach to explain why we need derivatives to measure speed at a single 'frozen' moment in time.
sections.example: An animation of 'Dash the Cheetah' sprinting. We know his average speed over 100m, but how fast is he moving exactly at the 2.5-second mark? This 'snapshot' speed is the derivative.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Slope of a Straight Line
sections.content: Briefly review the algebraic concept of slope (Rise over Run) for linear equations. Establish that for a straight line, the rate of change is constant everywhere.
sections.example: A character climbing a steady 30-degree ramp. The slope (m = Δy/Δx) is the same whether they are at the bottom or the top.

sections.title: Geometric Intuition: The 'Infinite Zoom' and Tangents
sections.content: Transition from straight lines to curves. Use the 'Microscope' analogy: if you zoom in enough on a curve, it looks like a straight line. Define the 'Tangent Line' as the line that just touches the curve at that point.
sections.example: A magnifying glass zooms into the curve of a roller coaster. As we zoom in 100x, 1000x, the curve flattens into a straight line. This 'local line' represents the derivative at that specific point.

sections.title: From Secant to Tangent: The Limit Visualized
sections.content: Show two points on a curve (a secant line). Gradually move the second point closer to the first until the distance (h) between them is nearly zero. This visualizes the limit definition of a derivative.
sections.example: Two dots on a parabola f(x) = x^2. As the second dot slides down the curve toward the first, the blue secant line pivots and transforms into a red tangent line.

sections.title: The Power Rule: Pattern Recognition
sections.content: Introduce the Power Rule (d/dx [x^n] = nx^{n-1}) as the 'shortcut' to finding the slope formula without doing complex limit calculations every time.
sections.example: A 'Magic Machine' where you drop in x^3 and out comes 3x^2. Visually demonstrate with x^2 (a parabola): the slope at x=1 is 2(1)=2, and at x=2 it is 2(2)=4. The graph's steepness matches the formula's output.

sections.title: Summary & Application: The Peak of the Mountain
sections.content: Recap that the derivative is the 'slope of the tangent.' Explain a key application: when the derivative is zero, the tangent line is horizontal, often indicating a peak or a valley.
sections.example: A hiker standing at the very top of a hill. At the peak, their path is momentarily flat (slope = 0). This is how engineers find the maximum height of a drone's flight path using derivatives.

storyboard.title: The Hook: The Cheetah's Instantaneous Speed
lecture_lines: Dash the cheetah sprints across the savanna.
Average speed is calculated over total time.
But how fast is he at this exact moment?
animations: Animate a cheetah sprinting quickly across the screen from left.
Freeze the cheetah's motion at exactly the 2.5-second mark.
Highlight the cheetah with a #00FF00 circle and label 'Instantaneous Speed'.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Slope of a Straight Line
lecture_lines: Imagine climbing a ramp with a steady incline.
The slope, rise over run, stays constant here.
A straight line has the same rate everywhere.
animations: Draw a character climbing a straight 30-degree ramp (#FFFFFF).
Show a Rise (#00FF00) and Run (#0000FF) triangle on the ramp.
Move the triangle along the ramp showing the ratio never changes.

storyboard.title: Geometric Intuition: The 'Infinite Zoom' and Tangents
lecture_lines: Now, let's look at a curving roller coaster.
The slope changes at every point along the track.
Zooming in closer, the curve begins to flatten.
Eventually, it looks just like a straight line.
This "local line" is the tangent to the curve.
animations: Draw a yellow (#FFFF00) roller coaster curve on a black background.
Mark a specific point P on the curve with a white dot.
Introduce a circular magnifying glass effect around point P.
Smoothly scale up the view inside the glass until the curve flattens.
Draw a blue (#0000FF) tangent line that perfectly matches the flattened curve.

storyboard.title: From Secant to Tangent: The Limit Visualized
lecture_lines: We start with two points on this parabola.
A secant line connects them to show average change.
Watch as we slide the second point closer.
The gap shrinks until it is nearly zero.
The secant transforms into a single-point tangent line.
animations: Plot a purple (#FF00FF) parabola y = x^2 on the screen.
Place two points, A and B, at different locations on the curve.
Draw a blue (#0000FF) secant line passing through both points A and B.
Slide point B along the curve until it almost overlaps with A.
Use ReplacementTransform to morph the blue secant into a red tangent.

storyboard.title: The Power Rule: Pattern Recognition
lecture_lines: Finding every slope using limits takes too long.
The Power Rule offers a magical shortcut.
For $x$ squared, the derivative is simply $2x$.
At $x$ equals one, the slope is two.
The formula predicts the curve's steepness perfectly.
animations: Display the formula d/dx[x^n] = nx^{n-1} in bright cyan (#00FFFF).
Animate a 'Derivative Machine' box in the center of the screen.
Move 'x^3' into the machine and show '3x^2' emerging as output.
Show a parabola where the slope at x=1 is labeled '2'.
Flash the labels at x=1 and x=2 to emphasize the pattern.

storyboard.title: Summary & Application: The Peak of the Mountain
lecture_lines: A zero derivative means the tangent is horizontal.
This happens at the very peak of a mountain.
Derivatives help us find the highest and lowest points.
animations: Draw a green (#00FF00) mountain profile with a hiker at the peak.
Place a horizontal white (#FFFFFF) tangent line at the mountain's peak.
Animate the text 'Slope = 0' flashing next to the horizontal line.
